ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r6.claim: Mawbiq means a place of destruction; the root describes perishing, and sins can destroy a person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r6.anchor: الموبق المهلك يقال: وبق يوبق وبقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r8.claim: The majority read yawm yaqūlu in third person, referring to God; other readers say naqūlu, God speaking to the idolaters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ويوم يقول بالياء أي الله. وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة ويحيى وابن أبي ليلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r9.claim: Calling the false gods God's partners reports the polytheists' claim, not a divine acknowledgment; the omitted objects of zaʿamtum are understood as 'them as My partners.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r9.anchor: وليس المعنى أنه تعالى أخبر أنهم شركاؤه ولكن ذلك على زعمكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r10.claim: The command to call the partners means to seek their help against punishment or ask them to intercede.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r10.anchor: لدفع العذاب عنكم أو للشفاعة لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r11.claim: The apparent referent of baynahum is the idolaters and their alleged partners; another view makes it the people of guidance and misguidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في بينهم عائد على الداعين والمدعوين وهم المشركون والشركاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r12.claim: The summons and failure to answer apparently happen literally; alternatively, the idolaters' realization that lifeless objects cannot help them is figuratively their calling without response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p191/r12.anchor: والظاهر وقوع الدعاء حقيقة وانتفاء الإجابة. وقيل: يحتمل أن يكون استعارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r1.claim: The majority pronounce shirkāʾī with a long vowel and possessive yāʾ; Ibn Kathīr and Meccan readers shorten it, and both are possessive forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور شركائي ممدودا مضافا للياء، وابن كثير وأهل مكة مقصورا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets al-bayn as connection, making the phrase the first object of jaʿalnā; on the adverbial reading it is the second object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: البين هنا الوصل أي وجعلنا نواصلهم في الدنيا هلاكا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk gloss mawbiqan as a place of destruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك: الموبق المهلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God placed destructive punishment between the idolaters and their alleged partners.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: جعلنا بينهم من العذاب ما يوبقهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر وأنس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r5.claim: They identify mawbiq as a valley in Hell flowing with blood and pus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر وأنس ومجاهد: واد في جهنم يجري بدم وصديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the barrier as enmity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says it is a gathering or assembly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r7.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: إنه المجلس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p192/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses it as an appointed meeting or promise.

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r1.claim: The author prefers that God Himself address the unbelievers on Judgment Day, though some say angels speak; God will appear to people in forms according to their beliefs, and reproachful speech is plausible after speaking to cursed Iblis.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r1.anchor: الأظهر هو الأول لأنه قد ثبت أن الله تعالى يتجلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r2.claim: Some say the command to call the alleged partners is delivered by angels.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يقول على ألسنة الملائكة

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r3.claim: God calls them His partners sarcastically, to shame their claim that they would intercede, and means everything worshipped besides Him.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r3.anchor: أضافهم إليه على زعمهم تهكما بهم وتقريعا لهم

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r4.claim: Their call for aid is described elsewhere as followers asking their supposed gods for relief.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r4.anchor: ذكر كيفية دعوتهم في آية أخرى {إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا}

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r5.claim: The partners do not rescue or benefit them, though this does not rule out a formal spoken reply; obedience matters before death, since their afterlife obedience to the command to call gains nothing.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r5.anchor: أي : لم يدفعوا عنهم ضرا ولا أوصلوا إليهم نفعا

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r6.claim: Al-Farra reads the worldly bond between worshippers and worshipped as becoming their destruction in the afterlife; the word between can mean that bond, as in 6:94.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r6.anchor: قال الفرآء : {وجعلنا} تواصلكم في الدنيا هلاكا في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r7.claim: Mawbiq may be the place or shared cause of destruction, such as Hell or an enmity as severe as destruction.
BURSEVI:v5p198#2/r7.anchor: وهو النار أو عداوة هي في الشدة نفس الهلاك

BURSEVI:v5p199/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199/r1.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p199/r1.claim: Al-Qamus defines mawbiq as a place of destruction, a valley in Hell, or anything separating two things.
BURSEVI:v5p199/r1.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الموبق كمجلس المهلك وواد في جهنم

BURSEVI:v5p199/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p199/r2.claim: The author prefers a separating barrier between worshippers and the worshipped, preventing intercession by angels, Jesus, or Ezra without precluding their being together; sharing the fire applies to those destined to enter it.
BURSEVI:v5p199/r2.anchor: يقول الفقير الظاهر أن المعنى على الثالث أي : جعلنا بينهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r1.claim: God addresses the unbelievers, directly or through an intermediary, to rebuke and confound them, telling them to call their claimed partners for help or intercession.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r1.anchor: أي الله تعالى للكفار توبيخا وتعجيزا بواسطة أو بدونها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r2.claim: The attribution of partners reflects their own claims that these beings were both partners and intercessors; the referents may be Iblis and his progeny or everything worshipped besides God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r2.anchor: والإضافة باعتبار ما كانوا يزعمون أيضا فإنهم كانوا يزعمون أنهم شركاء كما يزعمون أنهم شفعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r3.claim: Some exegetes take the partners as Iblis and his progeny, whose substitution as allies follows from obeying their whisperings; another reading permits every object worshipped besides God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r3.anchor: وقد جوز غير واحد هنا أن يكون الكلام بتقدير زعمتموهم شركاء والمراد بهم إبليس وذريته

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa, Yaḥyā, Ibn Abī Laylā, Ḥamza, and Ibn Muqsam read نقول with the majestic first-person plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة ويحيى وابن أبي ليلى وحمزة وابن مقسم ﴿ نقول ﴾ بنون العظمة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads شركاي with a shortened form attached to the first-person yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير / شركاي / مقصورا مضافا إلى الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r6.claim: Calling on the partners demonstrates the idolaters' intense attempt to obtain intercession, though they cannot rescue them; spelling out their failure mocks their inability to grasp the obvious.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r6.anchor: وفيه بيان بكمال اعتنائهم بإغاثتهم على طريق الشفاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r7.claim: موبق is a place of destruction derived from wabq, meaning to perish, and the callers and called beings share in that ruin, namely Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ موبقا ﴾ اسم مكان من وبق وبوقا كوثب وثوبا أو وبق وبقا كفرح فرحا إذا هلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Anas, and Mujāhid describe it as a valley in Hell flowing with blood and pus.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r8.anchor: وجاء عن ابن عمر وأنس ومجاهد أنه واد في جهنم يجري بدم وصديد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r9.claim: ʿIkrima describes a river of fire with dark, mule-sized serpents on its banks; when they surge toward the damned, they flee into the fire and call out.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه نهر في النار يسيل نارا على حافتيه حيات أمثال البغال الدهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain موبق as a place of destruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r10.anchor: وتفسير الموبق بالمهلك مروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وعن مجاهد وغيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets it as enmity, the cause of destruction, comparing it with ʿUmar's saying that hatred can be destructive.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r11.anchor: وعن الحسن تفسيره بالعداوة فهو مصدر أطلق على سبب الهلاك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r12.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r12.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas interprets موبق as a prison.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p298#2/r12.anchor: وعن الربيع بن أنس تفسيره بالمحبس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r1.claim: Some say the destruction-place or prison is a barrier between the idolaters and their alleged partners, ending their hope of receiving intercession.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r1.anchor: معنى كون الموبق أي المهلك أو المحبس بينهم أنه حاجز واقع في البين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r2.claim: Some who understand the word as a valley say God uses it to separate the people of guidance from the people of error, allowing the partners to include the honored figures mentioned by exegetes.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r2.anchor: وجاء عن بعض من فسره بالوادي أنه يفرق الله تعالى به بين أهل الهدى وأهل الضلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r3.speaker: الثعالبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r3.claim: Al-Thaʿālibī defines موبق as a distant barzakh; the great distance destroys their attempts to reach one another, and can separate Paradise's honored inhabitants from Hell's wicked ones.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r3.anchor: وقال الثعالبي في فقه اللغة الموبق بمعنى البرزخ البعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r4.claim: If جعلنا means made or turned, بينهم is a complement and موبقا its first object; if it means created, بينهم is attached or describes the object, fronted for the verse ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r4.anchor: على جميع ما ذكر ظرف وهو مفعول ثان لجعل إن جعل بمعنى صير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r5.speaker: الفراء والسيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Sīrāfī take البين to mean connection rather than separation: God makes their worldly connection a cause of ruin on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء والسيرافي البين هنا بمعنى الوصل فانه يكون بمعناه كما يكون بمعنى الفراق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r1.claim: Hamza reads the verb with first-person plural 'We say'; other readers have 'He says,' referring to God addressing people on Judgment Day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة بالنون والآخرون بالياء أي: يقول الله لهم يوم القيامة:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r2.claim: The claimed partners are idols; their worshippers call and seek their help, but they neither answer nor help them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r2.anchor: يعني الأوثان {الذين زعمتم} أنهم شركائي {فدعوهم} فاستغاثوا بهم {فلم يستجيبوا لهم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r3.speaker: عطاء والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r3.claim: Ata and al-Dahhak interpret the barrier between them as a place of destruction.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the mawbiq is a valley in the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو واد في النار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r5.claim: Mujahid says it is a valley in Hell.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r6.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r6.claim: Ikrima describes a river of fire in Hell whose banks hold snakes as dark as large pack animals.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو نهر في النار يسيل نارا على حافته حيات مثل البغال الدهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r7.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r7.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi says any barrier between two things is mawbiq; its root denotes destruction, as in making someone perish.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r7.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: وكل حاجز بين شيئين فهو موبق وأصله الهلاك يقال: أوبقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r8.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r8.claim: Al-Farra says worldly bonds between idolaters and idols become their destruction in the afterlife; bayn can mean connection, as in 6:94 on a nominative reading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: وجعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا مهلكا لهم في الآخرة، والبين على هذا القول التواصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r1.claim: The address to disbelievers is spoken by God; Hamza reads the verb with the first-person plural nun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r1.anchor: أي الله تعالى للكافرين وقرأ حمزة بالنون

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r2.claim: The alleged partners are those the disbelievers claim are God's partners and their intercessors who could ward off punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r2.anchor: أنهم شركائي وشفعاؤكم ليمنعوكم من عذابي

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r3.claim: Calling them partners repeats the disbelievers' own claim as a rebuke; it means anything worshipped besides God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r3.anchor: وإضافة الشركاء على زعمهم للتوبيخ والمراد ما عبد من دونه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r4.claim: An alternative identification of the alleged partners is Iblis and his descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r4.anchor: ما عبد من دونه، وقيل إبليس وذريته

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r5.claim: The disbelievers call on the alleged partners for rescue, but they give no aid.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r6.claim: The barrier between the disbelievers and their deities is a place of shared destruction, namely the Fire.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r7.claim: Alternatively, the barrier is enmity so severe that it is itself destruction; Baydawi compares it to Umar's saying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r7.anchor: أو عداوة هي في شدتها هلاك كقول عمر رضي الله عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r8.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r8.claim: Umar warns that love should not become consuming attachment, nor hatred a ruinous calamity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r8.anchor: لا يكن حبك كلفا ولا بغضك تلفا

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r9.claim: Mawbiq can be a place noun or verbal noun from the verb meaning to perish.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r9.anchor: اسم مكان أو مصدر من وبق يوبق وبقا إذا هلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r10.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r10.claim: If bayn means connection, their worldly bond becomes destruction for them on Judgment Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:52-53/r10.anchor: وقيل البين الوصل أي وجعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا هلاكا يوم القيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r3.claim: The shift to third person signals the false partners' distance from God's presence, while the earlier reference to the Prophet's Lord does not imply that they share His proximity.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r3.anchor: عادلا إلى مقام الغيبة , إشارة إلى بعدهم عن حضرته الشماء وتعاليه عما قد يتوهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r4.speaker: حمزة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r4.claim: Ḥamzah reads the phrase with the first-person plural, maintaining the preceding first-person style and adding an expression of majesty.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r4.anchor: وجرى حمزة في قراءته بالنون على أسلوب التكلم الذي كان فيه مع زيادة العظمة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r5.claim: God sarcastically tells them to summon the alleged partners; the wording shows the claimed partnership is only their false assertion.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r5.anchor: نادوا شركاءي } وبين أن الإضافة ليست على حقيقتها , بل هي توبيخ لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r6.claim: The alleged partners do not answer or even wish to answer, disregarding their worshippers and attending to their own concerns.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r6.anchor: فلم يستجيبوا لهم } أي لم يطلبوا ويريدوا أن يجيبوهم إعراضا عنهم استهانة بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r7.claim: Mawbiq is destruction or a place of destruction, a strong and enduring barrier separating worshippers from their partners.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p476/r7.anchor: وجعلنا بينهم } أي المشركين والشركاء { موبقا * } أي هلاكا أو موضع هلاك , فاصلا حائلا بينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p477/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477/r1.claim: Mawbiq's separation changes worldly affection and connection into hatred and rupture, as in the cited Quranic passages.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477/r1.anchor: لأن معنى ذلك كله أنه يبدل ما كان بينهم من الود في الدنيا والوصلة ببغض وقطيعة كما قال تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir transmits from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that mawbiq is a deep valley separating the guided from the misguided on Judgment Day.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.anchor: نقل ابن كثير عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : هو واد عميق فرق به يوم القيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī interprets mawbiq as enmity.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري : عداوة . وأما أخذه من اللفظ فلأن مادة وبق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.claim: The Quranic context depicts parties seeking one another's destruction and gathering at a barrier that separates them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r3.anchor: وأن كل فريق يطلب للآخر الهلاك , فاقتضى ذلك اجتماع الكل فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.claim: His lexical analysis says the root has eleven arrangements, all revolving around gathering; وبق especially implies an impediment between two things and carries force, permanence, preservation, and destruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r4.anchor: ولها أحد عشر تركيبا : واحد يائي : بقي , وستة واوية : قبو , قوب , بقو , بوق , وقب , وبق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.claim: The word's force and permanence follow from separation: someone blocked from what he needs perishes literally if the barrier is death, or potentially otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p477#2/r5.anchor: ترتيب وبق يدور على الحائل بين شيئينن ويلزمه القوة والثبات والحفظ والهلاك قوة أو فعلا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r1.claim: The author derives forms of قوب from circular digging and holes, linking them to enclosure, gathering, removal, eggs, hatching, shells, and calamities.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r1.anchor: ومن الواوي : قاب الأرض يقوبها وقوبها : حفر فيها شبه التقوير - لأن الدائرة أجمع ما يكون لغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r2.claim: Related terms for an egg, hatching, chick, and shell are connected to the rounded hole or to separation from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r2.anchor: والقائبة والقابة : البيضة - لأنها لتدويرها تشبه ذلك الحفر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r3.claim: قاب may mean approaching, fleeing, or splitting; قاب قوسين names a bow's measure and a distance on the bow.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r3.anchor: وقاب : قرب - لأن القرب مبدأ الجمع , وقاب : هرب , أي سلب القرب - ضد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r4.claim: Forms of بقو mean looking at, guarding, or waiting; preservation implies firmness and permanence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r4.anchor: ومن الواوي : بقاه بعينه : نظر إليه - فهو من الحفظ اللازم للجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r5.claim: The yāʾ form بقي means to remain and endure, opposite to perishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p478/r5.anchor: ومن اليائي : بقي الشيء بقاء : ثبت ودوام ضد فني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r1.claim: The root بوق covers a heavy burst of rain, recurring afflictions and evils, a hollow horn, falsehood, indiscretion, calamity, and a gathered bundle of greens.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r1.anchor: ومن واويه : البوقة : الجمع والدفعة من المطر الشديد أو المنكرة تنباق - أنها نزلت من وقبة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r2.claim: The same root's بوائق mean recurring afflictions or evil, while a hollow horn and its sound are associated with falsehood and revealing secrets.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r2.anchor: والبوائق : العوائد - لأنها جامعة لمن اعتادها , والبوائق : الشر - لأنه معلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r3.claim: The word وبق can also mean falsehood and fabricated speech, and the horn's hollowness explains related senses.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r3.anchor: والوبق أيضا : الباطل والزور - لأن صوته أشبع شيء بذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r4.claim: وقب centers on cavities and openings, including a water-filled rock hollow or well, bodily hollows, containers, and entering a hollow.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r4.anchor: والوقب والوقبة : نقرة في الصخرة يجتمع فيها الماء , وقيل : هي نحو البئر في الصفا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r5.claim: The root describes the moon entering an eclipse and the sun setting; disappearance is likened to entering a pit and being hidden from light.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r5.anchor: ووقب القمر وقوبا : دخل في الظل الذي يكسفه - كأنه حفرة ابتلعته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r6.claim: A foolish person is called وقب as though he were a container for everything heard, unable to distinguish good from bad; Thaʿlab gives a related sense of lowliness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r6.anchor: ورجل وقب : أحمق - كأنه وعاء لكل ما يسمع , لا أهلية له في تمييز جيده من رديئه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r7.claim: وبق and موبق mean to perish, a place of destruction, or anything intervening between two things; the barrier's separation is like a pit.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r7.anchor: ووبق - كوعد ووجل وورث وبوقا وموبقا : هلك , أي وقع فيه وقبة , أي حفرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r8.claim: The hamzated أبق describes a servant who leaves secretly or without fear, and related forms mean hiding, detention, or denying something.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p479/r8.anchor: ومن مهموزة : أبق العبد - كسمع وضرب ومنع - أبقا ويحرك - وإباقا - ككتاب : ذهب بلا خوف

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r1.claim: Mawbiq means a place of destruction.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {موبقا} يقول: مهلكا

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r2.claim: Mawbiq is a valley in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {موبقا} قال: واد في جهنم

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r3.claim: The barrier between idolaters and their supposed partners is a valley in Hell made of pus and blood.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r3.anchor: عن أنس في قوله: {وجعلنا بينهم موبقا} قال: واد في جهنم من قيح ودم

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r4.claim: It is a deep valley in the Fire separating guidance from error on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر في قوله: {وجعلنا بينهم موبقا} قال: هو واد عميق في النار فرق الله به يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r5.speaker: عمرو البكالي
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r5.claim: Mawbiq is a deep-bottomed valley in the Fire separating Muslims from everyone else at Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r5.anchor: عن عمرو البكالي قال: الموبق الذي ذكر الله واد في النار بعيد القعر يفرق به يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r6.claim: It is a river of fire in Hell whose banks hold dark snakes the size of mules; people flee them by plunging into the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {موبقا} قال: هو نهر في النار يسيل نارا على حافتيه حيات أمثال البغال الدهم

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r7.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r7.claim: Kaʿb names four valleys by which God punishes Hell's inhabitants: Ghaliz, Mawbiq, Atham, and Ghayy.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r7.anchor: عن كعب قال: إن في النار أربعة أودية يعذب الله بها أهلها: غليظ وموبق وأثام وغي

QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r8.claim: Idols neither benefit, harm, nor help; God will make their uselessness undeniable to end the worshippers' delusion that they bring nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r8.anchor: علم الحق - سبحانه - أن الأصنام لا تغني ولا تنفع ولا تضر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r1.claim: The verse may be linked to the command to prostrate in 18:50, with remember understood, or to 18:51, implying that neither partners were shown creation nor will they help on Judgment Day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم ( الكهف : 50 ) فيقدر : واذكر يوم يقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r2.claim: The passage shifts from denying the divinity of Satan and jinn to all idols worshipped by common polytheists, depicting their frustration and despair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r2.anchor: فهو انتقال من إبطال معبودية الشيطان والجن إلى إبطال إلهية جميع الآلهة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r3.claim: The argument denies divinity by denying a necessary consequence: partners that cannot benefit their worshippers cannot be gods, leaving worshippers in failure and despair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r3.anchor: الاستدلال على انتفاء الماهية بانتفاء لوازمها ، فإنه إذا انتفى نفعها للذين يعبدونها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r4.claim: Most readers use يقول in the third person, whose subject is God by context; Ḥamza reads نقول with the majestic plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r4.anchor: وقرأة الجمهور يقول } بياء الغيبة وضمير الغائب عائد إلى الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r5.claim: The scene is the Gathering, and the command is directed to polytheists, as الذين زعمتم indicates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r5.anchor: واليوم الذي يقع فيه هذا القول هو يوم الحشر . والمعنى : يقول للمشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r6.claim: Calling the idols partners before saying the people alleged this mocks and rebukes them; زعم then marks their claim as false.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r6.anchor: وقدم وصفهم بوصف الشركاء قبل فعل الزعم تهكما بالمخاطبين وتوبيخا لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r7.claim: Calling asks the idols to come for aid or intercession; responding means acknowledging the call and approaching, for example by saying لبّيكم.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r8.claim: The command to call the idols is literal but also exposes their falsehood; they call out in hope, and the immediate past-tense narration makes their failure seem instantaneous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r8.anchor: وأمره إياهم بمناداة شركائهم مستعمل في معناه مع إرادة لازمه وهو إظهار باطلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r9.claim: موبق means a place of destruction; here it is Hell, whose chasms God puts between worshippers and idols, or it is a circumstantial clause preparing for the sight of the Fire in 18:53.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p344/r9.anchor: والموبق هنا أريد به جهنم ، أي حين دعوا أصنامهم بأسمائهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r6.claim: The scene is a threat: God tells polytheists to call for help from partners they claimed; “my partners” means according to their claim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r6.anchor: وقوله ويوم يقول الآية وعيد، المعنى واذكر يوم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r7.speaker: طلحة ويحيى والأعمش وحمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r7.claim: These readers say “We say” in the first-person plural; most say “He says,” with God addressing the polytheists.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ طلحة ويحيى والأعمش وحمزة «نقول» بنون العظمة، وقرأ الجمهور بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r8.claim: Zaʿm usually reports uncertain, often false speech, though at best it means reporting while leaving responsibility with the speaker, as in Sibawayh’s “al-Khalil reported.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r8.anchor: وقوله شركائي أي على دعواكم أيها المشركون وقد بين هذا بقوله الذين زعمتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r9.claim: The idols’ failure to answer is most plainly literal, though it could be figurative: the polytheists’ recognition of idols’ impotence is like calling without response.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r9.anchor: ظاهره أن ذلك يقع حقيقة، ويحتمل أن يكون استعارة، كأن فكرة الكفار ونظرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وأنس بن مالك ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r10.claim: These authorities say mawbiq is a valley in Hell flowing with blood and pus; Anas says it separates Hell’s people from believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r10.anchor: قال عبد الله ابن عمرو وأنس بن مالك ومجاهد: هو واد في جهنم يجري بدم وصديد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan interprets mawbiq as enmity between them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن موبقا معناه عداوة وبينهم على هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r12.claim: Ibn Kathir and Meccans open the final yā in shirkāʾī; the majority use hamza, either fully articulated or softened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p523#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأهل مكة «شركائي» بياء مفتوحة، وقرأ الجمهور: «شركائي» بهمزة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r1.claim: Some take “between them” as a location separating believers from unbelievers or polytheists from idols; Ibn ʿAbbas explains mawbiq as destruction, while a meeting place is weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس موبقا معناه مهلكا بمنزلة موضع وهو من قولك وبق الرجل وأوبقه غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r2.claim: The strongest reading makes mawbiq a noun: their connection itself is destructive; “between them” can be the first object of “made.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r2.anchor: والأظهر فيه أن يكون اسما، بمعنى جعلنا تواصلهم أمرا مهلكا لهم،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r1.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r1.claim: Hamza reads naqūlu with first-person plural nūn, placing the address on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة نقول بالنون يعني يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r2.claim: The partners are called God’s only according to the polytheists’ own claim; they are summoned to avert punishment or intercede.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r2.anchor: أضاف الشركاء اليه على زعمهم والمراد نادوهم لدفع العذاب عنكم أو الشفاعة لكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r3.claim: The parties separated by the barrier may be polytheists and their partners, or people of guidance and people of error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r3.anchor: في المشار إليهم قولان أحدهما انهم المشركون والشركاء والثاني أهل الهدى وأهل الضلالة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Dahhak gloss mawbiqan as a place of destruction; Ibn Qutayba specifies a ruinous divide between polytheists and idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r4.anchor: مهلكا قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك وقال ابن قتيبة مهلكا بينهم وبين آلهتهم في جهنم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God places between them a punishment that destroys them; the root means to perish.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r5.anchor: جعلنا بينهم من العذاب ما يوبقهم أي يهلكهم فالموبق المهلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r6.claim: Al-Farra says their worldly connection becomes their ruin in the afterlife; bayn can mean connection, as in the variant at 6:94.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r6.anchor: جعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا موبقا أي مهلكا لهم في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r7.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r7.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr says mawbiq is a deep valley separating people of error and guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r7.anchor: أن الموبق واد عميق يفرق به بين أهل الضلالة وأهل الهدى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r8.claim: Anas ibn Malik and Mujahid say mawbiq is a valley in Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r8.anchor: أنه واد في جهنم قاله انس بن مالك ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r9.anchor: ان معنى الموبق العدواة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r10.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r10.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas interprets mawbiq as a prison.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r10.anchor: أنه المحبس قاله الربيع بن أنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets mawbiq as an appointment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r12.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r12.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains the open-mīm form: it is a fixed name for a prison, not derived by analogy; its root is God’s causing someone to perish.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p155#2/r12.anchor: أنه اسم موضوع لمحبس في النار والأسماء لا تؤخذ بالقياس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r1.claim: On Judgment Day God publicly rebukes polytheists by telling them to summon the partners they claimed in worldly life to save them; he links this to 6:94.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r1.anchor: مخبرا عما يخاطب به المشركين يوم القيامة على رؤوس الأشهاد تقريعا لهم وتوبيخا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r2.claim: The claimed partners will not respond; he links this to 28:64, 46:5–6, and 19:81–82, where the false gods become enemies of their worshippers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p169#3/r2.anchor: وقال {ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and others explain mawbiqan as a place of destruction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة وغير واحد: مهلكا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r2.claim: Through ʿAmr al-Bakkālī, Qatāda reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that it is a deep valley separating the people of guidance from those of error on Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r2.anchor: حدث عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: هو واد عميق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r3.claim: Qatāda also identifies mawbiqan as a valley in Hell.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r4.claim: Anas ibn Mālik describes it as a valley in Hell filled with pus and blood; Ibn Jarīr transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r4.anchor: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول في قول الله تعالى: {وجعلنا بينهم موبقا} قال: واد في جهنم، من قيح ودم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī interprets mawbiqan as enmity.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r6.claim: The apparent contextual meaning is destruction, though it could be a valley in Hell or another barrier: the polytheists and their claimed gods cannot reach one another, with ruin and terror between them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r6.anchor: والظاهر من السياق هاهنا: أنه المهلك، ويجوز أن يكون واديا في جهنم أو غيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r7.claim: Alternatively, if “between them” refers to believers and disbelievers, the verse describes their separation; he connects this reading to 30:14, 30:43, 36:59, and 10:28–30.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p170/r7.anchor: عائدا إلى المؤمنين والكافرين، كما قال عبد الله بن عمرو

JISHUMI:v6p4433/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r5.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r5.claim: Hamza reads ويوم نقول in the first-person plural, attributing the statement to God.
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: ويوم نقول بالنون مضافا إليه تعالى،

JISHUMI:v6p4433/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r8.speaker: ثعلب
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r8.claim: Mawbiq may mean anything that separates things, or destruction.
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r8.anchor: قال ثعلب: كل شيء حال بين شيء فهو موبق،

JISHUMI:v6p4433/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda says mawbiq means appointed time.

JISHUMI:v6p4433/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r10.speaker: ابن عرفة
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r10.claim: Ibn Arafa explains mawbiq as a holding place or prison.
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عرفة: موبقا محبسا، يقال: أوبقه: حبسه

JISHUMI:v6p4433/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r11.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r11.claim: Al-Kisa’i gives two vowel patterns for wabiqu.
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r11.anchor: وحكى الكسائي: وبق يبق بفتح الباء في الماضي وكسرها في المستقبل،

JISHUMI:v6p4433/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r12.claim: In the hadith about crossing the bridge, mawbiq because of sins can mean detention or destruction.
JISHUMI:v6p4433/r12.anchor: وفي الحديث المرور على الصراط: ومنه الموبق بذنوبه يحتمل الحبس ويحتمل الهلاك.

AKHFASH:v2p431/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p431/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p431/r1.claim: موبقا follows the pattern of موعد and derives from وبق يبق; أوبقته means I caused it to perish.
AKHFASH:v2p431/r1.anchor: وقال {موبقا} مثل {موعدا} من "وبق" "يبق" وتقول "أوبقته حتى وبق".

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r1.claim: The verb ‘he says’ is read with either yāʾ or nūn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r1.anchor: بالياء والنون . وإضافة الشركاء إليه على زعمهم : توبيخا لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r2.claim: Calling them ‘partners’ is a rebuke that adopts their own claim; the partners meant are the jinn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r2.anchor: وإضافة الشركاء إليه على زعمهم : توبيخا لهم وأراد الجن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r3.claim: Al-mūbiq means a place of ruin, from verbs meaning to perish or cause to perish; alternatively it is a noun for a shared valley in Hell, a place of ruin and severe torment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r3.anchor: الموبق : المهلك ، من وبق يبق وبوقا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says al-mūbiq means enmity so intense that it is ruin, illustrated by a poetic warning against love becoming excessive or hatred destructive.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن { موبقا } عداوة . والمعنى : عداوة هي في شدتها هلاك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says al-bayn means connection: the partners’ worldly connection becomes ruin for them at the Resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء : البين الوصل أي : وجعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا هلاكا يوم القيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the partners are angels, ʿUzayr, Jesus, and Mary, with al-mūbiq meaning the distant barrier separating their places in Hell and the highest gardens.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد الملائكة وعزيرا وعيسى ومريم ، وبالموبق : البرزخ البعيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r7.claim: Fa-ẓannū means they became certain; muwāqiʿūhā means they will encounter and fall into the Fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r7.anchor: فظنوا } فأيقنوا { مواقعوها } مخالطوها واقعون فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r8.claim: Maṣrifan means a way of turning aside; the author cites a poetic line addressed to Zuhayr as a witness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#2/r8.anchor: مصرفا } معدلا . قال : أزهير هل عن شيبة من مصرف ;

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r1.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r1.claim: Mawbiq can mean a place of assembly, according to al-Rabiʿ.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r2.claim: Mawbiq can mean a place of destruction; Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Dahhak give this gloss, which poetry attests with أبق and موبق.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : مهلكا , قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك , قال الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains that the allies' worldly solidarity becomes their destruction in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : جعل تواصلهم في الدنيا مهلكا في الآخرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r4.claim: Mawbiq can mean an appointed meeting place.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r6.claim: Mawbiq can mean a valley in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r6.anchor: الخامس : أنه واد في جهنم , قاله أنس بن مالك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r7.claim: A later, unnamed authority says it is a valley separating Paradise from Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p316#2/r7.anchor: السادس : أنه واد يفصل بين الجنة والنار , حكاه بعض المتأخرين .

FARRA:v2p146/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p146/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p146/r7.claim: Mawbīq means that their worldly connection becomes a cause of destruction in the afterlife; another view makes it a valley in Hell.
FARRA:v2p146/r7.anchor: وقوله: وجعلنا بينهم موبقا [52] يقال: جعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا (موبقا)

MUJAHID:v1p377#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p377#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p377#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the mawbīq between the idolaters and their alleged partners as a valley in Hell.
MUJAHID:v1p377#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ موبقا ﴾ قال الموبق واد في جهنم

MUQATIL:18:52-54/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r1.claim: God tells the polytheists to call the partners they claimed were gods; they cannot answer that they are gods.
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r1.anchor: يقول: فسألوهم، فلم يجيبوهم بأنها آلهة

MUQATIL:18:52-54/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r2.claim: The barrier between the polytheists and their alleged partners is a deep valley in Hell.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r1.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r1.claim: Hamza reads ‘We say’ with the letter nūn where the other reading has ‘He says.’
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r1.anchor: وبالنون حمزة ﴿ نادوا ﴾ ادعوا بصوت عال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r2.claim: نادوا means call aloud; the alleged partners are the jinn, called ‘My partners’ only according to the idolaters’ claim, to rebuke them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ نادوا ﴾ ادعوا بصوت عال ﴿ شركائي الذين زعمتم ﴾ انهم فيكم شركائي ليمنعوكم من عذابي واراد الجن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r3.claim: موبقا can mean destruction or its place, a shared valley in Hell where all perish; another interpretation is a distant barrier between the idolaters below and their supposed partners in the highest gardens.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا ﴾ مهلكا من وبق يبق وبوقا إذا هلك أو مصدرا كالموعد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r4.claim: Alternatively, the barrier separates the people of Hell from angels, ʿUzayr, and Jesus in the highest gardens.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p17#4/r4.anchor: أو للملائكة وعزيزا وعيسى والموبق البرزخ البعيد أي وجعلنا بينهم أمدا بعيدا لأنهم في قعر جهنم وهم في أعلى الجنان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r1.claim: Mawbiqan is a destroyer between the idolaters and their gods in Hell; awbaqahu means his sins ruined him, as in 42:34.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r1.anchor: {وجعلنا بينهم موبقا} أي: مهلكا بينهم وبين آلهتهم في جهنم. ومنه يقال: أوبقته ذنوبه. وقوله: {أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا}

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r2.claim: Mawbiqan is also said to mean a rendezvous or appointed meeting.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p269/r2.anchor: أي: مهلكا بينهم وبين آلهتهم في جهنم. ومنه يقال: أوبقته ذنوبه. وقوله: {أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا} (1) ويقال: موعدا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r3.claim: The call to summon partners is addressed to idolaters; they cannot answer or protect them. Hamza, Yahya, and Isa read نقول; the others say يقول, matching شركائي.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r3.anchor: أي اذكروا يوم يقول الله: أين شركائي؟ أي ادعوا الذين اشركتموهم بي فليمنعوكم من عذابي.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r4.claim: Mawbiq is a valley of pus and blood or a barrier between believers and unbelievers; another view puts it between idols and worshippers, while Ibn al-Arabi defines it as any separator.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r4.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: هو واد في جهنم من قيح ودم.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r5.speaker: مجاهد ونوف البكالي وعكرمة وعطاء والضحاك وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r5.claim: Mujahid and Nauf say valley in Hell; Ikrima gives a fiery river and snakes; Ata and al-Dahhak say destruction, and Abu Ubayda an appointed destruction. The lexicon gives root forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:51-52/r5.anchor: وذكر ابن وهب عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى: «موبقا» قال واد في جهنم يقال له موبق.

RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r5.claim: Hamza reads first-person plural ‘We say,’ linked to God's earlier ‘We said to the angels’; the other readers use third-person ‘he says.’
RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة : ( نقول ) بالنون عطفا على قوله : { وإذ قلنا للملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r6.claim: The clause can mean ‘remember the day We say,’ linked to the earlier command to the angels.
RAZI-FULL:v21p118/r6.anchor: واذكر يوم نقول عطفا على قوله : { وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا

RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to make idolaters call their alleged partners, meaning the jinn they worshiped, for aid and intercession; they receive no answer or benefit. Another verse gives their words to the partners.
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r1.anchor: أي ادعوا من زعمتم أنهم شركاء لي حيث أهلتموهم للعبادة

RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines mawbiq as destruction or a place of annihilation; one account places a ravine in Hell between pagans and the angels or Jesus they worshiped.
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الموبق المهلك من وبق يبق

RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan interprets mawbiq as enmity so intense that it is ruinous, supporting it with a poem about love and hatred.
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن : ( موبقا ) أي عداوة والمعنى عداوة هي في شدتها هلاك

RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra explains the word as their connection or bond, which becomes their ruin on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r4.anchor: قال الفراء البين المواصلة أي جعلنا مواصلتهم في الدنيا هلاكا

RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation is a distant barrier between unbelievers in Hell's depths and the angels or Jesus in the highest gardens, so remote that a traveler perishes crossing it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p118#2/r5.anchor: الموبق البرزخ البعيد أي جعلنا بين هؤلاء الكفار وبين الملائكة وعيسى

STUDYQURAN:18:52/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r1.claim: God challenges those who associated partners with Him to call them for intercession or aid as a rebuke; the alleged partners abandon, disown, or cannot help them.
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r1.anchor: to intercede for them or to help them

STUDYQURAN:18:52/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r2.speaker: IK, Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r2.claim: Mawbiq may mean a place of destruction or a valley of Hell into which idolaters are cast.
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r2.anchor: between them may refer to a place of destruction

STUDYQURAN:18:52/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r3.speaker: R, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r3.claim: Alternatively, mawbiq may mean the enmity that becomes manifest between idolaters and the partners they ascribed to God.
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r3.anchor: Others suggest that mawbiq may refer here to the enmity that will manifest itself

STUDYQURAN:18:52/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r4.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the gulf the vast barzakh between Makkan idolaters who associated angels with God, in Hell, and the angels in the highest celestial realm.
STUDYQURAN:18:52/r4.anchor: Still others interpret the gulf between them as referring to the vast intermediate expanse

NAHHAS:v2p461/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p461/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p461/r1.claim: The supposed divine partners are those people made partners in divinity and worship; they call on them to rescue them from torment or repay their worship.
NAHHAS:v2p461/r1.anchor: أي الذين جعلتموهم شركاء في الألوهة والعبادة فنادوهم ليخلصوكم

TABATABAI:18:52/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:52/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:52/r1.claim: This is a third reminder: on Judgment Day God exposes the broken bond between idolaters and alleged partners by telling them to summon them; their failure to answer proves they are no partners.
TABATABAI:18:52/r1.anchor: هذا تذكير ثالث يذكر فيه ظهور بطلان الرابطة بين المشركين وبين شركائهم يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:18:52/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:52/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:52/r2.claim: Mūbiq is a place of destruction; although commentators take it as Hell or a region of it, the author rejects that because partners include angels, prophets, and saints, not only rebellious jinn and humans.
TABATABAI:18:52/r2.anchor: وقد فسر القوم هذا الموبق والمهلك بالنار أو بمحل من النار يهلك فيه الفريقان

TABATABAI:18:52/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:52/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:52/r3.claim: The gap is the annihilation of the supposed relationship, not of either party; the call across distance hints at their separation, as in 6:94 and 10:28.
TABATABAI:18:52/r3.anchor: فلعل المراد من جعل موبق بينهم إبطال الرابطة ورفعها من بينهم

TABRISI:18:50/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50/r2.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:18:50/r2.claim: Ḥamzah reads the later phrase with first-person plural nūn; the others use third-person yāʾ.
TABRISI:18:50/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ويوم نقول بالنون والباقون بالياء

TABRISI:18:50/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:50/r3.claim: The nūn reading connects with the preceding first-person expression; yāʾ fits a sentence break and the sense that God says to summon the partners.
TABRISI:18:50/r3.anchor: من قرأ نقول بالنون حمله على ما تقدم في المعنى

TABRISI:18:50/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:50/r4.claim: The yāʾ reading is stronger because the address says summon My partners; a nūn reading would more naturally say Our partners.
TABRISI:18:50/r4.anchor: وهذا يقوي القراءة بالياء لأنه لو كانت بالنون

TABRISI:18:50-52/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50-52/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:50-52/r9.claim: On Judgment Day, idolaters are told to call partners they claimed would ward off punishment; those partners will not answer or help.
TABRISI:18:50-52/r9.anchor: يريد يوم القيامة يقول الله للمشركين وعبدة الأصنام

TABRISI:18:50-52/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50-52/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:18:50-52/r10.claim: The mawbiq is a deep ravine separating people of guidance from people of misguidance.
TABRISI:18:50-52/r10.anchor: وهو اسم واد عميق فرق الله به سبحانه بين أهل الهدى وأهل الضلالة عن مجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:18:50-52/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50-52/r11.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
TABRISI:18:50-52/r11.claim: Alternatively, the mawbiq is a barrier between deities and worshippers; the author says the supposed deities are placed with unbelievers in Hell.
TABRISI:18:50-52/r11.anchor: وقيل: بين المعبودين وعبدتهم موبقا أي حاجزا عن ابن الأعرابي

TABRISI:18:50-52/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50-52/r12.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:18:50-52/r12.claim: Their worldly bond and friendship in unbelief becomes a cause of destruction in the Hereafter; this is also reported from Qatādah and Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:18:50-52/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه جعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا موبقا

TABRISI:18:50-52/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50-52/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:18:50-52/r13.claim: Mawbiq can mean enmity that is itself destructive.
TABRISI:18:50-52/r13.anchor: وقيل: موبقا عداوة عن الحسن فكأنه قال عداوة مهلكة

TABRISI:18:50-52/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:50-52/r14.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:18:50-52/r14.claim: Mawbiq is a valley of pus and blood in Hell.
TABRISI:18:50-52/r14.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك أنه قال: الموبق واد في جهنم

THALABI:v6p177/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p177/r3.speaker: حمزة
THALABI:v6p177/r3.claim: Hamza reads ‘on the day He says’ with nūn; the others read yāʾ, fitting ‘my partners’ rather than ‘our partners.’
THALABI:v6p177/r3.anchor: ويوم يقول نادوا قرأ حمزة بالنون. الباقون بالياء لقوله: شركائي

THALABI:v6p177/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p177/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p177/r4.claim: Mawbiqan is interpreted as a deep Hell valley, boiling fluid, a river of fire, enmity, destruction, or an appointed place; its root means ruin.
THALABI:v6p177/r4.anchor: وجعلنا بينهم يعني بين الأوثان وعبدتها. وقيل: بين أهل الهدى والضلالة موبقا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r1.claim: The speaker of 'on the day He says' is God. Most read yaqulu in third person to agree with 'My partners'; Hamza reads naqulu in first person plural in line with the preceding first-person 'I was not.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ويوم يقول} أي: الله تعالى، وقراءة العامة: بالياء لقوله: {شركائي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns the Day of Resurrection; commentators say God will tell polytheists to call their supposed partners to save them from punishment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'those you claimed' refers to what they claimed in worldly life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r4.speaker: أنس، مجاهد، عبد الله بن عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r4.claim: Anas, Mujahid, and Abdullah ibn Umar say the mawbiq is a valley in Hell filled with pus and blood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r4.anchor: قال أنس: (هو واد في جهنم من قيح ودم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r5.speaker: نوف البكالي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r5.claim: Nawf al-Bikali says the mawbiq is a valley separating the people of error from the people of faith.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r5.anchor: وقال نوف البكالي: (هو واد بين أهل الضلال وبين أهل الإيمان)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r6.speaker: البكالي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r6.claim: Al-Bikali also says it is a barrier separating those who profess 'there is no god but God' from everyone else; Ata's report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-A'rabi likewise define it as a barrier between two things.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r7.claim: On the barrier reading, 'between them' refers to believers and disbelievers, but the author notes no known derivation supports mawbiq meaning barrier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r7.anchor: إلى الفريقين من المؤمنين والكافرين، وليس يعرف للموبق بمعنى الحاجز اشتقاق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas in al-Walibi's report glosses mawbiq as destruction; Qatada, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, al-Suddi, and semantic authorities agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي: (مهلكا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r9.claim: Al-Farra says the mutually reinforcing connection they had in this world becomes their destruction in the next; on this analysis, 'between them' is an object referring only to the polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: (يقول: جعلنا تواصلهم في الدنيا موبقا، أي: مهلكا لهم في

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq says God placed destructive torment between them; bayn is adverbial and mawbiq is a verbal noun meaning destruction, hence a cause of ruin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي جعلنا بينهم من العذاب ما يوبقهم أي: يهلكهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r11.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak explicitly glosses mawbiq as destruction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p51#2/r11.anchor: ونص الضحاك على لفظ الهلاك فقال في قوله: {موبقا}: (هلاكا)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r1.claim: On Judgment Day, God tells idolaters to call their partners to protect them from His punishment, but the partners do not answer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r1.anchor: يقول الله تعالى يوم القيامة: ادعوا الذين أشركتم بي ليمنعوكم من عذابي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r2.claim: A barrier will separate the idolaters from those who profess that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r2.anchor: فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم } بين المشركين وأهل لا إله إلا الله { موبقا } حاجزا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r6.claim: Mawbiq is glossed as a valley in Hell; another view takes it to mean destruction, making the worldly bond between idols and worshippers fatal.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r6.anchor: قوله: {ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا} [الكهف: 52] واد في جهنم. وقال بعضهم: موبقا، مهلكا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r7.claim: Qatada reports that Nauf al-Bikali related from Abdullah ibn Amr that mawbiq is a deep valley separating the guided and astray on Resurrection Day.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن نوفا البكالي حدث عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: هو واد عميق فرق به يوم القيامة بين أهل الهدى وأهل الضلالة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p191#2/r8.claim: Another explanation takes the wording as “We caused them to perish,” meaning We put them in the Fire.

SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r1.claim: يوم is governed by اذكر: remember the day when We say this will happen.
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r1.anchor: أي: ويوم نقول يجري كيت وكيت.

SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r2.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r2.claim: He reads نقول with the first-person plural, matching ما أشهدتهم; the other readers use third-person ياء because God’s name was just mentioned.
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r2.anchor: بنون العظمة مراعاة للتكلم في قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r3.claim: موبقا may be the first object of جعل with the preposed phrase between them as second; alternatively جعل takes one object and the phrase attaches to it or circumstantially modifies موبقا.
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r3.anchor: مفعول أول للجعل، والثاني الظرف المقدم.

SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r4.claim: موبق means ruin or destruction, with the verb used for perishing and for a sin bringing destruction.
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r4.anchor: الموبق: المهلك، يقال: وبق يوبق وبقا، أي: هلك

SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r5.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r5.claim: He interprets the phrase as God making their connection a ruin, taking البين to mean connection rather than a locative interval; on this parse بينهم is the first object and موبقا the second.
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r5.anchor: فجعل البين بمعنى الوصل، وليس بظرف كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r6.claim: موبقا is apparently a verbal noun, though it may denote a place.
SAMIN-DURR:18:52/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مصدرا وهو الظاهر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r1.claim: The supposed partners are attributed to God only according to the polytheists’ own claim.

ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r2.claim: Mawbiq means something that destroys or brings ruin; the verb is reported in dialects as wabiqu or yabiqu, and the first form is preferred.
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r2.anchor: جعلنا بينهم من العذاب ما يوبقهم، أي يهلكهم، والموبق المهلك.

ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r3.claim: Among forms of the verb meaning perish, wabiqu is the primary form, alongside reported dialect forms wabiqu/yabiqu and wābiq.
ZAJJAJ:v3p295/r3.anchor: يقال وبق الرجل يوبق، وبقا ويقال ييبق، وبائق

ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n58/r1.claim: The supposed partners are beings people imagined to share in God's divinity; Asad links the phrase to 6:22.
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n58/r1.anchor: Lit., "those partners of Mine whom you supposed [to exist]": see note 15 on 6:22.

ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r1.claim: One interpretation makes the gulf a divide of unreality between sinners and the blasphemous figments of their imagination.
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r1.anchor: wide gulf of unreality that separates those sinners from the blasphemous figments of their imagination

ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari and Razi
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r2.claim: Zamakhshari and Razi offer an alternative: the gulf separates sinners from saintly people they worshipped, who never claimed divine status; Asad considers this more probable.
ASAD-NOTES:18:52#n59/r2.anchor: Zamakhshari and Razi in one of their alternative interpretations, with specific mention of Jesus and Mary

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verse recalls the idolaters’ deprivation on Judgment Day, when a pit of destruction separates them from the idols they invoked.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This verse reminds them of their deprivation on that day. The pit of destruction will obstruct the idolaters and their idols from one another

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r1.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza alone reads “We say” with nūn; the others use the third-person yāʾ form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة وحده: (نقول) بالنون وقرأ الباقون بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r2.claim: The nūn reading coheres with the preceding first-person statement, “I did not take the misguiders as helpers.”
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p151#2/r2.anchor: قول حمزة (نقول) إن قبلها: وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r1.claim: Yaqūlu with yāʾ reports the command through the Prophet from God; nūn makes God speak in the first person.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r1.anchor: يقرأبالياء والنون فالحجة لمن قرأه بالياء أنه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r2.claim: Qubulan with both vowels rounded is plural of qabīl and means group by group; with kasra on qāf and fatḥa on bāʾ it means visibly and face to face.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r2.anchor: يقرأ بضم القاف والباء وبكسرها وفتح الباء فالحجة لمن ضم أنه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r3.claim: Some linguists say qabīlah means a tribe descended from a father and qabīl means a group, citing the demand to bring God and the angels qabilan.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة القبيلة بنوأب والقبيل الجماعة واستدل بقوله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r4.claim: A poem uses qabīl for the opposing host, which is certain to be first to prevail when the two armies meet.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p225#2/r4.anchor: وبقول الشاعر جوانح قد أيقن أن قبيلهم إذا ما التقى الجمعان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p391/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p391/r6.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p391/r6.claim: Ḥamza alone reads yawm naqūlu with nūn; the other readers use yāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p391/r6.anchor: 18 واختلفوا فى الياء والنون من قوله ﴿ ويوم يقول نادوا ﴾ 52

QIRAAT-ER:18:52:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:52:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:52:3#1/r1.claim: The first-person plural reading makes God speak directly, replacing third-person narrative report with divine announcement.
QIRAAT-ER:18:52:3#1/r1.anchor: First person plural ""We say"" — shifts speaker from third-person God to direct divine voice

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ موبقا ﴾ قال هلاكا

ITQAN:v4p378/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.claim: Ghayy, Atham, Mwbq, Saʿir, Wayl, Saʾil, and Suhaq are valleys in Hell.
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.anchor: وغي وأثام وموبق والسعير وويل وسائل وسحق أودية في جهنم

ITQAN:v4p378/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ITQAN:v4p378/r8.claim: Anas ibn Malik says the Mwbq placed between them is a valley in Hell made of pus.
ITQAN:v4p378/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك في قوله ﴿ وجعلنا بينهم موبقا ﴾ قال واد في جهنم من قيح

ITQAN:v4p378/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r9.speaker: عكرمة
ITQAN:v4p378/r9.claim: Ikrima gives a different gloss for Mwbq: it is a river in the Fire.
ITQAN:v4p378/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ موبقا ﴾ قال هو نهر في النار

ITQAN:v4p378/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r12.speaker: كعب
ITQAN:v4p378/r12.claim: Kaʿb says four valleys in the Fire punish its inhabitants: Ghaliz, Mwbq, Atham, and Ghayy.
ITQAN:v4p378/r12.anchor: عن كعب قال في النار أربعة أودية يعذب الله بها أهلها غليظ وموبق وأثام وغي

ITQAN:v2p318/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p318/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p318/r9.claim: Mawbīq means a place or cause of destruction.

DAMGHANI:v1p173/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r4.claim: The command to call the alleged partners means to ask whether they are gods; they fail to answer as gods.
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r4.anchor: الخامس : الدعاء بمعنى الاستفهام ( والمناداة له ) قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.claim: The prepositional lām is normally distinguished from the lām of emphasis by kasra, avoiding confusion in forms such as إن هذا لعلى.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.anchor: لو فتحوها في الإضافة لالتبست بلام الابتداء

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.claim: With an attached pronoun, the lām is opened because that form cannot be nominative and so cannot be mistaken for lām of emphasis.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.anchor: أن هذا الإضمار لا يكون للرفع ويكون للجر

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.claim: The attached-pronoun form أعطيتكموه is compared with an overt object to explain the analogy, though Sībawayh notes the constructions are not identical.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.anchor: شبهوا به قولهم أعطيتكموه في قول من قال أعطيتكم ذلك

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولكلعبداللهمالثمتقوللكما.claim: Yūnus reports أعطيتكمه and أعطيتكمها by analogy with an overt noun; the ordinary pronominal form is more common and better known.
